Linux boot 33.0 s; service active 18 s after kernel start. NOTE: 'SSH back' (229 s, then 285 s) is NOT a readiness metric -- ssh to this node runs over Tailscale, so it measures re-registration; the service was serving 144 s before SSH answered. selfmodel.db runs e29f450b4356, cc40cd8ca4a8

measurement: Aged instance (~7.5 h, 5.8 G peak, 314.9 M swap): SIGTERM did NOT stop it; ran to the 15 s cap and needed SIGKILL, result 'timeout'. Fresh instance, same signal, 180 s cap: deactivated successfully in 0.246 s
notes: State-dependent, but the stall now reproduced a SECOND time during an actual reboot (n=2) -- the trigger (uptime/swap/requests served) is NOT isolated. Consequence: systemd's DEFAULT 90 s stop timeout was stalling every shutdown, which is most of A43's 199 s pre-Linux cost; TimeoutStopSec=15 caps it. KillSignal=SIGINT was tried and is WORSE (15 s cap on a fresh instance vs 0.246 s for SIGTERM) -- reverted. selfmodel.db run 8b8a7eb57d8b

feature: Reboot cost is dominated by the OS
measurement: Attributed from the persistent journal: OS shutdown 16 s, Tegra firmware/bootloader 107 s, Linux boot 33.0 s. Firmware alone is 66% of the 161 s between reboot command and a booted kernel+userspace
notes: So OS-side tuning has a hard floor here: even a zero-cost shutdown and instant boot would still cost 107 s of firmware. The 76 s already recovered via TimeoutStopSec is most of what the OS can give. research/cluster A43/A44; selfmodel.db run cc40cd8ca4a8
